full_details: The book has a rehearsal at the Theatre this morning. You are not there. You are at Field's for an hour, chewing on the right side, for a quire of Rochelle crown at the trade price. He shows you a forme with one turned letter and a dropped line, and what it costs to mend a fault no reader will thank. You know the trade. A cue changed in one part is two other rolls changed, and you have been treating the king's rolls as if paper were weather. He says so before you can. Jacqueline points at the pile in the passage. You both move it. The afternoon is The Shrew, and you play. The part is not named, and the journal does not keep the performance. At home you con Gaunt with half a mouth and a clove. Gilbert carries the sixty shillings, sewn in canvas, to the Bell for tomorrow's carrier. Four lines go with him. Alse hears "this England" and asks the honest question. You say both. Mistress Ansell calls her down. Gilbert, going, leaves you the ribbon if the king fails. The ledger says the money went by him. It does not say what is left.
one_sentence: You paid fourpence halfpenny for paper, moved a pile out of Jacqueline's way, and sent sixty shillings to the Bell by Gilbert.
title: Paid fourpence halfpenny, and sent sixty shillings by Gilbert
